context: First composite built from individually-tested signals. Inputs: two VALIDATED NEGATIVE SCREENS (NSI Q5, Quality Q5 -- confirmed factor-drag removal, not alpha), and two SUGGESTIVE POSITIVE TILTS that individually failed the standalone bar (Inverse 20D momentum: L-S t=2.12 but L-O alone t=1.10; Breakout: L-O t=1.66, cost-sensitive at raw 87.6%/wk turnover). This test asks whether combining them produces something that clears the standalone bar (t>2.0, cost<3%/yr) that none of the pieces cleared alone, and specifically whether it beats the exclusion-filter-only baseline (Portfolio D) on factor-adjusted alpha rather than just replicating Portfolio D's factor-tilting result (D vs SPY: t=0.34, not significant).
universe: Full Sharadar PIT eligible universe, same liquidity/history/sector filters as all prior strategies (excl. Finance/Real Estate).

step1_hard_exclusions.nsi_q5: Bottom quintile (Q5, by the existing net_share_issuance.py ascending-sort convention) on trailing-365-day sharesbas (MRQ) percent change. Recomputed at every weekly rebalance from the same PIT fundamentals logic already used monthly in net_share_issuance.py.
step1_hard_exclusions.quality_q5: Bottom quintile (Q5, by the existing quality.py descending-score convention) on the 6-component quality composite (roe, roa, gm, dte, icr, cfe -- mean of cross-sectional percentile ranks). Recomputed at every weekly rebalance from the same PIT fundamentals logic already used monthly in quality.py.
step1_hard_exclusions.note: Excluded names receive no composite score and are not eligible for the portfolio at that rebalance, regardless of how they'd score on A/B.

step2_scores.score_A_inverse_20d: -1 * percentile_rank(trailing 20-trading-day return), percentile rank computed cross-sectionally among the non-excluded universe at that rebalance. Low recent return -> percentile rank near 0 -> score_A near 0 (favorable, relatively high). High recent return -> percentile rank near 1 -> score_A near -1 (unfavorable, relatively low).
step2_scores.score_B_breakout_stability: Binary. 1 if close_t > max(close[t-126..t-1]) at BOTH the current weekly rebalance AND the immediately preceding weekly rebalance (2 consecutive weekly closes each a new 126-trading-day high); 0 otherwise. No volume filter in this formula -- the composite's 2-consecutive-week persistence requirement is the turnover fix in place of volume confirmation; this is a deliberate deviation from the standalone breakout test's definition, not an oversight.
step2_scores.composite_score: 0.7 * score_A + 0.3 * score_B, computed only for non-excluded stocks. Weights preregistered and fixed for this run; not to be tuned after seeing results.

construction.step3_portfolio: Sort remaining (non-excluded) stocks by composite_score descending. Hold the top quintile (top 20% of non-excluded names). Equal weight. Rebalance weekly, Friday close formation and execution (consistent with momentum/reversal/breakout tests).

factor_model: FF5 + UMD (6-factor), long-only convention (nets RF) -- this is a long-only single portfolio, no long-short leg is defined for the composite itself.
cost_model: 10bps round-trip on weekly turnover of the held top-quintile portfolio. Cost flag if annualized cost > 3%/yr -- reported prominently before alpha if it fires.
multiple_testing_correction: None -- single composite hypothesis, standard t>2.0 threshold for holdout advancement. The multiple-testing burden was incurred during individual signal development, not repeated here.

falsification_criteria.primary_pass_advance_to_holdout: alpha t>2.0 AND annualized cost<3%/yr AND RMW loading positive AND small-cap alpha > large-cap alpha
falsification_criteria.suggestive_composite_only: t between 1.5 and 2.0, OR cost between 3-5%/yr with positive alpha
falsification_criteria.falsified: t<1.5, OR alpha negative, OR cost>5%/yr

benchmarks.secondary: equal-weight full universe, Portfolio A from the exclusion-filter test (test1_portfolio_A.csv), dev-period subset -- active alpha of composite over A via long-short-convention regression on (composite - A)
benchmarks.tertiary: SPY, raw CAGR difference over the aligned dev-period months

critical_comparison: Portfolio D (exclusion filters only, no positive tilts) produced +2.15%/yr raw over SPY but t=0.34 factor-adjusted -- that was factor tilting, not alpha. This composite must be judged against that bar explicitly: does adding the two suggestive positive tilts on top of the same two exclusions produce materially higher, more significant factor-adjusted alpha than the exclusions alone? If not, the composite adds nothing beyond Portfolio D.
size_tercile_analysis: Within-size quintile formation: re-rank the non-excluded universe by composite_score independently within each of 3 market-cap terciles (Small/Mid/Large), take each tercile's own top quintile, run the same FF5+UMD long-only regression per tercile on its monthly returns. Prediction: small-cap alpha > mid-cap alpha > large-cap alpha (consistent with every individual signal's size pattern so far). Falsified if large-cap shows the strongest alpha.
constraints: Development period only; 2017-2025 holdout not touched in this run.
Weights (0.7/0.3) and signal definitions are fixed pre-run and will not be adjusted after seeing results.
If cost flag fires, it is reported before alpha numbers, not after.
If the result is weak, report it as weak -- no rescue attempts (re-weighting, re-defining signals, dropping bad weeks) after the fact.

amendments.reason: RMW criterion incorrectly specified for price-signal-dominated composite. Buying recent losers (inverse 20D) structurally loads negatively on RMW by construction -- not evidence of factor replication. The correct factor-independence test is residual alpha t-stat and R2, both of which the composite passes. RMW criterion removed and replaced.
amendments.procedural_note: This amendment was written after the development result was already known (alpha t=2.75, R2=0.781, RMW=-0.289) and specifically because the original RMW criterion failed. Even though the mechanistic argument for the change is plausible on its own merits, it was not proposed before seeing which criterion would fail -- it is a post-hoc criterion change, precisely the kind of move the original preregistration's 'do not rescue weak results' constraint was written to prevent. Recorded here for the record so any reader of the holdout result that follows can weight it accordingly: the development-stage gate was loosened until the development data cleared it, before holdout was consumed.
